Tone conventions vary slightly between Yoruba dialects and older missionary sources.

manannan.scriptFamily: Old Irish / Middle Irish in Insular script

signs.name: Manannán 'son of the sea'
signs.note: The name is traditionally derived from Manann, a figure linked to the Isle of Man; the final -án is a diminutive or patronymic suffix.

signs.name: mac Lir 'son of Lir'
signs.note: Ler / Lir is an old personification of the sea in Irish tradition.

steps: Old Irish was written in the Latin alphabet using Insular minuscule from the early medieval period.
The name appears in the Ulster Cycle and Mythological Cycle as Manannán mac Lir, 'son of Lir (the sea)'.
The acute accent on the final á marks a long vowel in modern scholarly convention.
The Unicode restoration Manannán preserves the long vowel; the ASCII form flattens the name.
provenance.etymology: Irish Manannán, traditionally 'son of the sea' (mac Lir); the first element may connect to the Isle of Man.
provenance.semantics: Sea, otherworld, mist, and liminality; a guide between worlds.
uncertainties: The etymology of the first element Manann- is debated.
Insular script spelling varies across manuscripts.
provenance.dnsNotes: The Unicode restoration Manannán uses the acute accent to mark the long final vowel; the ASCII form loses this length marker.

dazhbog.timePeriod: Old East Slavic, c. 10th–12th c. CE

signs.note: Cyrillic letter Д represents voiced alveolar /d/.

signs.name: az / a
signs.note: Short /a/ vowel.

signs.note: Voiced postalveolar fricative /ʒ/.

signs.name: buki / b
signs.note: Voiced bilabial /b/.

signs.note: Mid back vowel /o/.

signs.note: Voiced velar stop /ɡ/.

steps: The name is attested in East Slavic chronicles as Дажьбогъ (Dažĭbogŭ) and in the Primary Chronicle.
It is usually analyzed as daždĭ 'rain, gift' + bogŭ 'god', hence 'giving god' or 'rain god'.
The modern Unicode restoration Dažbog uses the caron ž; the medieval Cyrillic spelling includes the reduced jer vowels ь and ъ.
The Cyrillic form is not registrable in .com; the Latin transliteration Dažbog is.
provenance.etymology: Old East Slavic daždĭ 'gift, rain' + bogŭ 'god'; 'the giving god'.
provenance.semantics: Sun, wealth, giving; a solar deity whose gifts include rain and prosperity.
uncertainties: The exact pre-Christian form and function of Dažbog are debated; chronicles were compiled after Christianization.
The relationship between Dažbog and other Slavic solar deities (e.g., Svarog) is uncertain.
provenance.dnsNotes: The Unicode restoration Dažbog uses the caron ž; the Cyrillic form is not supported in .com.

jizo.timePeriod: Heian period – present, c. 9th c. CE –

signs.name: chi / ji 'earth, ground'
signs.note: The left-hand earth radical (土) gives the meaning; the right-hand component supplies the sound.

signs.name: zō 'storehouse, treasury'
signs.note: Combines the grass radical (艹) with 臣 and 戈; denotes a repository, womb, or treasury.

steps: Sanskrit Kṣitigarbha ('Earth Treasury' or 'Earth Womb') was translated into Chinese as 地藏 (Dìzàng).
Japanese borrowed the compound as 地蔵, read in Sino-Japanese as Jizō.
Hepburn romanisation writes the long vowel with a macron: Jizō.
The ASCII form jizo loses the length mark, collapsing the distinction between short and long ō.
The Unicode restoration Jizō is registrable in .com; the kanji form is not supported in the .com IDN table.
provenance.etymology: Sanskrit kṣiti 'earth' + garbha 'womb, embryo, interior'; rendered into Chinese as 地藏 'earth store' and borrowed into Japanese as 地蔵.
provenance.semantics: Earth Treasury Bodhisattva; guardian of children, travelers, firefighters, and beings in hell.

attestations.reference: Mizuko Jizō cult, Sai no Kawara legends

uncertainties: The Sanskrit phonology of Kṣitigarbha is simplified in the Japanese form; retroflex and aspirated consonants are not preserved.
The Japanese reading is a Sino-Japanese on'yomi, not the indigenous kun'yomi.
provenance.dnsNotes: The Unicode restoration Jizō preserves the long vowel; the kanji form is not registrable in .com.
